key_insight: OpenDeepThink scales LLM reasoning breadth by sampling many candidate reasoning traces in parallel and overcomes noisy pointwise judging by aggregating pairwise comparisons with a Bradley–Terry model to reliably pick the best solutions.
problem_solved: Selecting the best answer from multiple parallel reasoning candidates at test time is unreliable because single-shot LLM judgments are noisy and biased; this selection bottleneck prevents effective breadth-based compute scaling.
method: Parallel breadth: generate a population of diverse reasoning traces in parallel at test time.
Pairwise evaluation: obtain pairwise preference judgments between candidates (via LLM comparisons or human/automatic proxies).
Bradley–Terry aggregation: fit a pairwise preference model to produce global scores/ranking and select or combine top candidates (optionally iterate to refine the population).
impact: Provides a robust, compute-efficient way to leverage parallel sampling for better LLM reasoning without needing a perfect verifier, improving accuracy and reliability for practitioners using test-time compute scaling.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: parallel sampling → pairwise comparisons → Bradley–Terry aggregation → selected answer

paper_title: OpenDeepThink: Parallel Reasoning via Bradley--Terry Aggregation
paper_authors: Shang Zhou, Wenhao Chai, Kaiyuan Liu, Huanzhi Mao, Qiuyang Mang
